title: Associated points of a module and the relative assassin
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Define $\operatorname{Ass}_X(\mathcal F)$ as the set of $x\in X$ for which the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is an element-annihilator associated prime [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes] of the stalk $\mathcal F_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], using the stalk module [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. If $f:X\to S$ is a morphism of schemes, put $\mathcal F_s=(f.\operatorname{fiber}\iota_s)^*\mathcal F$ on the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] [def-pc-module-pullback]. Define $\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)=\bigcup_{s\in S} i_s(\operatorname{Ass}_{X_s}(\mathcal F_s))\subseteq X$, where $i_s:X_s\to X$ is the fibre projection. Equivalently, $x$ belongs precisely when its canonical point in $X_{f(x)}$ belongs to $\operatorname{Ass}_{X_{f(x)}}(\mathcal F_{f(x)})$. For quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent] this is the relative assassin of Stacks Tag 05AT.
